digest.component_or_area: bridge command surface and tracker sync orchestration
propositions: Bridge redesign consolidates fragmented Jira-specific operator surface into one provider-neutral Python-first command interface (canonical: `rebar bridge` with verbs setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, resume) while retaining all legacy contracts and compatibility adapters.

Argument-less `reconcile` remains dry-run (non-mutating) and argument-less `bridge sync` is the canonical mutating command; canonical exit codes are 0/1/2 with legacy 3/4/75 translations preserved through explicit compatibility adapters.

Bridge functionality is exposed through three shared Python-owned interfaces (CLI, Python library, MCP server) and three install paths (brew, pip, MCP-server/uvx) with no surface implementing private bridge semantics.
Pause state is remote-persisted with reason and remains readable by mixed-version fleets; destructive repair and normal bridge operation no longer require GitHub-specific `gh` CLI dependency.
Python core (src/rebar/_store/push.py) owns tickets-branch CAS retry, fetch-and-merge recovery, strict failure classification, and terminal push budget; workflow-local CAS loops are removed.

Bridge is runner-neutral across local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments with shared code-derived exit behavior, secrets vocabulary, and timeout policy; provider wrappers remain thin declarative shells validated as test artifacts.
